otherReaderScope.predicateLimits: Succeeded and explicit failed/subset predicates can logically imply I1 terminal predicate, subject to planner parameterization. All-state latest, state<>running, pending/running-only and mixed active subsets do not imply the entire partial-index predicate. Do not assert universal non-admission of composite queries containing eligible subqueries.

writerObligations.effect: New pending row is outside I1. Replaced pending→cancelled with updated_at inserts terminal entry; account generation BEFORE INSERT trigger remains authoritative.

Pending/running changes mostly outside I1; failed→cancelled inserts/rekeys. Heartbeat locked_at-only and payload-only promotions do not add I1 columns, but real checkpoint also changes already-indexed updated_at. Current corpus has no eligible running writer.

Running→succeeded or failed creates terminal entry; failed→pending removes one; pending→cancelled creates one, failed→cancelled/recent terminal timestamp changes rekey it. Preserve fenced retries, notification resolution and cleanup triggers; never execute these owners in index-read proof.

Cancellation cascades can change active→terminal rows. Connection deletion FK SET NULL moves I1 leading key; user deletion removes rows. Full domain effects make destructive owner experiments wider than a safe microcontrol.

Generation pin is BEFORE INSERT. AFTER UPDATE OF state triggers prune Trakt staging and provider snapshots on succeeded/cancelled; connection generation/status triggers prune corresponding staging/snapshots. Actual trigger/function/RLS metadata must be checked before any future row-write controls.

futureWriteOptions.option: One or a few existing terminal actual rows, exact ordinary recency-only UPDATE under savepoints for I0 and I1; preserve existing user/connection/generation/state/payload. Any derived changed timestamp is an explicit controlled metadata schedule, not a natural provider workload. Obtain review for exact expression before execution.
futureWriteOptions.proves: Complete RETURNING/postvalues/side-effects equality and descriptive indexed timestamp maintenance/BUFFERS/WAL for that actual row. Logical full-table/sequence/catalog restoration after outer rollback.
futureWriteOptions.doesNotProve: Natural completion/claim/retry/heartbeat throughput, successful-writer HOT rate, physical restoration or whole app write cost. Updated_at is already indexed, so it cannot establish additional HOT eligibility loss.

futureWriteOptions.option: For causal physical writer/index overhead use two fresh matched disposable actual-data clones, I0 vs I1, source/target guards and per-clone schema/data equality. Apply reviewed controlled metadata writes to existing rows in corresponding order, record EXPLAIN BUFFERS/WAL and xact update/HOT counters only if verified; drop only generated targets.
futureWriteOptions.proves: A cleaner bounded physical maintenance comparison than sequential rollback phases with warming/dead tuples; current indexes remain in both.
futureWriteOptions.doesNotProve: No naturally missing active/failed state cohort is invented; no worker/provider work. Clone copy/free-space/cache differences still limit throughput/HOT extrapolation; full production migrations/provenance and storage-scale remain separate.

futureWriteOptions.option: Use a genuinely retained running/failed writer cohort if one becomes available; invoke only a reviewed bounded owner with provider calls forbidden and full rollback/equality. Do not convert terminal rows into fictitious running jobs to satisfy a test.
futureWriteOptions.proves: Potentially meaningful current heartbeat/checkpoint/transition contract with real stored state; unavailable now.
